text:
FTR Homework #7: After reading some more posts regarding FTR scattered around the forum and after re-reading markepedia article on FTR, I now understand what important barriers are.

Bro Staurum also gave an awesome guide: without FTR, there is no FL without break there is no FTR without a zone or price barrier, there is no break without price movement, there is no zone or price barrier Not gonna skip to the FL just yet, but with that hint, and a few more hints on the previous posts, I've come to realize that firstly a zone/price barrier must be created first, before looking for their breaks and only afterwards, we should look for FTRs. Probably this is obvious for most of you, but not me. Yes, I'm a very slow learner What I've been doing is finding FTRs first before assessing the importance of the significant barriers that created them. Obviously bro Staurum has been trying to pound that we should do the reverse, i.e. find significant barriers FIRST, then find FTRs, not the other way around. A few posts from you actually mentioned it, but somehow I failed to understand the correctly For now, I define "important barriers" as important SR lines that gets respected many times in the past. Thank you for being super patient with me brother With that in mind, I'm giving this FTR stuff another try. Not gonna give up until I get the all clear to go to the next section, the glorious FLs.

Below is the historical chart of CHF/JPY. What I am still unclear though is the FTR that I marked with "not sure if this is an FTR...." from the historical chart. Is that an FTR or just a price cap? What confuses me is that price engulfed the previous FTR, signaling that price wants to go up, but then it breaks the low that started the upswing. I've read that of an engulf happens first, then the next engulfs to the opposite side are FOs. Any hints on this matter?

Here are the FTRs for that pair's monthly chart. I have marked significant barriers first with the purple horizontal lines, then marked up the FTRs for them.

Chart 7-1: The possible entry on D1 Chart Chart 7-2: Using FTR to trade SR It seems very convenient for the IT to blast through important SRs with a large range candle to hide the kink in the LTF. Since I have no LTF data below H4 on this pair, I assume the FTR is somewhere in the orange box. If there is no observable FTR (kink) inside the wide range candle, then as expert RTMers mentioned, we should use the entire candle body that broke the SR as the FTR (did I get this wrong?)

author: Frosty
text:
FTR Homework #8 As for the homework, I'll continue with LTF charts from here on to fast forward my learning process, i.e. see the outcomes of my analysis faster.

I do have FT2 on my PC, but the data is 4 digit, not 5 digit. Gotta find how to fix that first before it is able to be fully utilized.

Main Chart: Important SR Selection / Reasons: LTF View of CPPAZ 1: LTF View of CPPAZ 2: LTF View of CPPAZ 3: LTF View of FTB to FTR 11: What I have learned / I think I have learned from this homework: 1. CPPAZ is a form of PAZ. Nothing new here for all of you, but it certainly is new to me. It is called a PAZ for a reason. The best CP acts similar to a "Pole". The spaces between FTRs are called PAZs. The equation then is: CPPAZ = PAZ = Poles. As always, please correct me if I am wrong on this. 2. Based on the findings in the above point, the edges of CPPAZ, i.e. the MPL of the base of CP and the MPL of the last S/D in the CP, are limits of the flag that will be created above and below. It could be significant bounce, or it can be a minor pause and small bounce. The FTR after the break of these two important zones are important FTRs (found this already in a previous HW, but will type this again to see if I got this correctly). 3. FO zone is the space between DP and the important FTR after a break of significant FTR on the left, provided that the MPL of the DP hasn't been spiked yet.

What I need to understand more: 1. How to differentiate whether the retrace after engulf of important FTR will go to DP to engulf or to the FTR itself. This is the ultimate confusion for me as of now. Sometimes price reacts to the MPL, Sometimes it reacts to FTR, Sometimes it reacts to the DP to engulf. For example on bro Staurum's chart above, bounce can actually happen in blue or in red box. The choice are many. One possible solution that I thought of is to look on LTFs to find a reaction such as the one described in markepedia, e.g. QMs and Diamonds. Would anyone please share a little hint on this? Thank you in advance.

2. Important barriers. The latest way I define significant important barriers are after the engulf of SRs that are created after buyers/sellers are trapped, like the chart above. After an engulf of important SRs in the manner described before is the way I marked FTRs right now. Also, I will mark FTRs created after the engulf of the important FTRs on the left created in this way as well. Is this the correct way to do it?

I just can't seem to understand this. Please tell me if I am moving backwards. I'm very amazed at all of you for getting these stuff very quickly, lol. More reading to do here. Thank you all for your continued guidance

author: staurum
text:
your progress, in my opinion, is great. I'm so excited to see that you are already including CPPAZ. I'm happy to see it. My suggestion would be to keep it simple. means, while you have noted CPPAZ in the charts, and because we are doing FTR homework here, i think it's best to include only PAZ that is between FTRs. Reason? U know price barrier, engulf, FTR, all these make up PAZ already.

IF's mantra: "Yes peeps, keep it simple. PAZs are the spaces between FTRs. They're the spaces in which flags form."

Ah-huh,, that's right. FLAGS. so u know that this homework is so critical for you. Because after this, FL will come naturally to you. no question about it.

In regards to your questions, it would be so much better to understand the answers to those when you complete the FL reading and homework. I'm not saying that you shouldn't know the answer now, because other RTM members can give you the answers straight away. But, from my experience, this homework for you already serves its purpose.

You have to believe you are moving forward. Please put the doubts aside. Just a bit of encouragement: So, to recap my thoughts into this, understand S/R and other possible barriers in any form (and also the meaning behind them in terms of orders (supply & demand)), understand engulf as the Real Action to show imbalance (and entrance into another zone), recognise FTR as decision to target the next decision (the next FTR targeted by the engulf PA) and look at the PAZ as possible path for price to travel after the engulf to the next prior opposite engulf/FTR. Next planet: PAZ
